author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Aaron Judge returned to the New York Yankees lineup Tuesday night after an 84-game absence, starting in right field and batting third against the Colorado Rockies.

The Yankees reinstated their captain from the 60-day injured list on Monday. Judge had not played since May 31 because of a stress fracture in his right first rib. The injury, which he believes occurred on a diving play in late April, was initially diagnosed as a bone bruise before later scans showed the fracture.

Judge resumed playing catch in mid-August after earlier running and light baseball work. He returned without a minor-league rehabilitation assignment. Before the injury, the three-time American League Most Valuable Player was batting .248 with 17 home runs and 38 RBIs in 59 games.

His return comes during a tight American League East race. Entering Tuesday, New York was 81-62, four games behind Tampa Bay and two ahead of Boston. Those standings are a dated pregame snapshot, not live results. The immediate question is how quickly Judge can regain game timing after missing most of the summer.
dek: The New York captain started in right field Tuesday after recovering from a stress fracture in his right first rib.
headline: Aaron Judge returns to Yankees lineup after 84-game absence
